title: Order approved steward proposals in the plan like other items
summary: Drain currently approves in-limit steward proposals up front (approve_all) and works them before the plan, starving urgent queued requests. Make approved proposals plan entries ordered by dependency, priority, rung, age, with priority defaulting to normal unless the role or a priority record says otherwise; drain then follows the plan, and `athena plan` lists them in place. Audience: operators running `athena drain` and `athena plan`.

defaults_applied.how: Tests for drain order and plan listing; fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests pass.
Criteria check order of work and plan output.
Fix ordering by putting proposals into the plan, not special-casing the one proposal.
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy, fmt.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Approval still happens in drain, but approved proposals' jobs are merged into the plan and ordered rather than worked first.
Priority for a proposal comes from its role or a priority record; absent either it is normal.
No governance files need to change.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new drain test (run with cargo test -p athena-cli drain) with an approved in-limit proposal and an urgent queued request works the urgent request first, and fails on the old behavior.

A test shows the plan (Plan::build / the plan command path) lists an approved proposal at its ordered place by dependency, priority, rung, then age, defaulting to normal priority, with role or priority-record overrides honored.
Drain no longer works approved proposals ahead of the plan; approved proposals are ordered by the same rules as other items and job-limit/budget handling still applies.
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test pass.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the fix for a reader outside the project.

out_of_scope: Changing proposal approval limits or rung rules
departures: Touches drain ordering and plan logic with new tests across two crates; costlier than the reference median.
urgent_reason: Stops drain from spending both job slots on a failing low-priority proposal, cutting wasted failed attempts.
hard_reason: Changes drain's work ordering and the plan that gates which jobs run, so a mistake is costly and hard to see.
